name: immunity-wars
description: The Immunity Wars — cooperative immunology board game, digital edition

scripts.coverage:corpus: vitest run --config vitest.coverage.config.ts --coverage tests/equivalence/src/spread.test.ts -t "600 recorded bot games"
scripts.coverage:generators: vitest run --config vitest.coverage.config.ts --coverage tests/equivalence/src/spread.test.ts tests/equivalence/src/actions.test.ts tests/equivalence/src/queries.test.ts tests/equivalence/src/construct.test.ts
scripts.comment:test:balance: Checks this engine against the MEASURED bands in tests/balance/bands.json. Calibrating is a different, deliberate command (`npx tsx tests/balance/metrics-run.ts`) and deliberately NOT this one — a harness that recalibrated on every run would overwrite its own reference and could never fail. Wiring this into CI is Task F's.
scripts.comment:measure:query-payload: P2.1 decision C. Sizes the precomputed answers to all 22 UI queries against viewState, on real command-phase states, with the distribution per difficulty and the per-query decomposition. Reuses E1's instrument and E's game driver. REPORTS ONLY — nothing gates on it.
scripts.comment:measure:selection-cost: P2.1 decision C, the two conditions on the selection-scoped ruling. Times a selection-triggered view rebuild against the brief §4 redraw budget, and measures whether the same scoping applies to productionBreakdown. REPORTS ONLY.
scripts.comment:test:property: The fast tier already runs inside `pnpm test` via turbo. This is the >=10,000-game tier PHASE1_BRIEF.md section 9 asks for: slow, on demand, and exiting non-zero if any invariant finished having checked nothing. Same two-tier arrangement as the equivalence corpus. Wiring it into a CI tier is Task F's.
scripts.comment:test:manifest-controls: Mutates tests/suites.json six ways and requires manifest.test.ts to redden EXACTLY the assertions each mutation targets — not merely to go red, which would only prove the file is read. Deliberately NOT in `pnpm test`: it shells out to vitest, and a suite that recursively runs itself takes forever. Run it when the manifest or its schema changes.
scripts.comment:ci:selftest: Mutates one file, runs one gate, requires it to FAIL WITH THE RIGHT DIAGNOSTIC, and reverts. A CI pipeline that has never gone red is not known to work, and the usual way to prove it — pushing a broken commit — marks the branch history forever. Not in `pnpm test`: it shells out to the gates, including a full typecheck and lint per control.
scripts.comment:docs:check: The documentation sweep, as a check rather than a habit. CLAUDE.md said 'Current phase: Phase 1' for the whole first session of Phase 2 and ROADMAP.md agreed with it; a stale phase marker is not wrong enough to notice, so it survives. Checks the phase marker resolves and agrees with the brief it names, that every test package reaches tests/suites.json, and that every relative markdown link resolves. It does NOT read prose. Runs inside pnpm verify.
scripts.verify: pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm format:check && pnpm boundaries && pnpm docs:check && pnpm test
scripts.comment:seam:homes: P2.1 step 2. Classifies the 49 names v2_ui.html reads out of the engine into the three homes Phase 2's boundary rule leaves open, from the engine's own module grouping rather than from a second hand-written list. REPORTS ONLY — exits non-zero on a name with no home or a cross-check disagreement, and the query group is a decision for Shantanu, not an output of this script.
